tichitt-tradition.name: Tichitt tradition
tichitt-tradition.summary: A proto-Mande culture (2200–200 BCE) in what is now Mauritania, known for hierarchical settlements, farming and metallurgy at sites like Dhar Tichitt.

nok-culture.name: Nok culture
nok-culture.summary: An ancient population in what is now Nigeria, named for the village where its terracotta sculptures were first found in 1928, existing from roughly 1500 BCE to 1 CE.

bura-culture.name: Bura culture
bura-culture.summary: Iron Age archaeological culture, dated from around the 3rd to 13th century CE, centered in the lower Niger River valley of Niger and Burkina Faso, known for distinctive clay, iron and stone artifacts including early terracotta equestrian statuettes.

kintampo-complex.name: Kintampo Complex
kintampo-complex.summary: A West African prehistoric culture active roughly 2500 to 1400 BCE, established by Saharan agropastoralists and marking a shift from pastoralism to settled life, known for early figurative art, stone tools and structures.

djenn-djenno.name: Djenné-Djeno
djenn-djenno.summary: Ancient urban site in Mali's Niger River Valley, occupied from about 250 BC to 1400 AD, among the oldest known cities in West Africa and evidence of early long-distance trade.

soninke-people.name: Soninke
soninke-people.summary: A West African Mande-speaking ethnic group who founded the ancient empire of Ghana (Wagadou), around 200 to 1240 CE, later spreading widely as traders.

ghana-empire.name: Ghana Empire
ghana-empire.summary: An ancient West African empire based in what is now southeast Mauritania and western Mali, first mentioned in writing in 830 CE; it became a vassal of the Mali Empire in the 13th century.

akreijit.name: Akreijit
akreijit.summary: A town in central Mauritania founded in the mid-19th century by herders, near numerous archaeological sites investigated by later expeditions.

dia-mali.name: Dia
dia-mali.summary: A small town in the Inland Niger Delta of Mali, part of an ancient three-settlement site that predates nearby Djenné and Timbuktu and offers insight into early West African urbanization.

kaduna-state.name: Kaduna State
kaduna-state.summary: State in northwest Nigeria home to the Nok civilization (c. 1500 BC to 500 AD) and later part of the Sokoto Caliphate; became capital of the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate.

akan-religion.name: Akan religion
akan-religion.summary: The traditional beliefs of the Akan people of Ghana and eastern Ivory Coast, called Akom, featuring a senior god and many lesser gods, often blended today with Christianity.

yoruba-religion.name: Yoruba religion
yoruba-religion.summary: The traditional religious and spiritual system of the Yoruba people of West Africa, now the largest indigenous African belief system, with millions of followers.

odinani.name: Odinani
odinani.summary: The traditional religious and cultural belief system of the Igbo people of southeastern Nigeria, centered on a supreme deity with a pantheon of lesser gods and spirits.

serer-religion.name: Serer religion
serer-religion.summary: The original religious beliefs of the Serer people of the Senegambia region in West Africa, centered on a supreme deity called Roog and a cult of ancestors.

gao.name: Gao
gao.summary: A city in Mali on the River Niger, once a major trans-Saharan trade hub; it became capital of the Songhai Empire under Sunni Ali (1464–1492) after earlier being part of the Mali Empire.

kanem-bornu-empire.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
kanem-bornu-empire.summary: A long-lived empire around Lake Chad, founded around 700 CE and sustained by trans-Saharan trade, later re-centered from Kanem to the Bornu region after the 14th century.
